Investor positioning in silver is experiencing violent swings:

Speculative investors sold -$2.3 billion in silver futures over the 5 weeks ending November 3rd, according to CFTC data.

This was driven by -$2.6 billion in new short positions, partially offset by +$300 million in new longs.

Hedge funds and commodity trading advisers (CTAs), alongside smaller traders such as retail investors, accounted for most of the sales, with each group reducing exposure to silver futures by ~$1.4 billion.

As a result, aggregate net long speculative positioning fell to +$8.0 billion, its lowest since January 2025.

Since its January 2026 peak, this figure has dropped by more than -$16.0 billion.

Are investors overly bearish on silver?

The dollar has climbed to a new 19-month high, which could spell trouble for Japan.

Markets now see a December Fed hike as almost certain, and higher US rates keep pulling money into the dollar.

The other side of that trade is the yen. With Japan's rates still near zero, it's sliding towards 160 per dollar, and Tokyo's top currency official says the moves are "too rapid".

160 is where Japan stepped in back in 2024, selling dollars to buy yen and knocking dollar/yen down around 3% in a single day.

So 160 is the line to watch: an intervention there can knock the dollar back against the yen in a single session.
